pokemonCenter.name: Pokemon Center Tokyo Station & Tokyo DX
pokemonCenter.note: Optional on arrival — both centres ~10 min apart. Tokyo Station opens 10:00, Tokyo DX 10:30. Skip if tired; more PC days ahead.

place.name: Ameyoko Market
place.summary: A lively post-war market street under the Yamanote tracks — street food, dried goods, sneakers, and bargain snacks. Less polished than department stores, very local energy.
highlights: Sample grilled seafood skewers and fresh fruit
tips: Cash still preferred at smaller stalls
Go before 17:00 when stalls start closing
Watch your belongings — it gets crowded on weekends (today is quieter midweek)
place.photoNote: Colourful stall awnings and narrow alleys — allow extra time for photos.

place.name: Ueno Park (exterior stroll)
place.summary: One of Tokyo’s oldest public parks — ponds, shrines, and wide paths. Today is a gentle preview; full museum visit on Day 4.
tips: Benches throughout — good rest stop for seniors
Early October: greenery with occasional cosmos flowers, not yet peak autumn colour

meal.name: Uogashi Nihon-Ichi Ueno Okachimachi
meal.note: Affordable sashimi option near Ameyoko — order piece-by-piece at the counter (¥100–300 per piece). Quick, no reservation needed. Alternative to a sit-down lunch if you arrive hungry before exploring.

meal.name: Gyukatsu Motomura Ueno
meal.note: From your saved list. Deep-fried beef you finish on a hot stone — hearty after travel. Expect 20–40 min queue at peak; go early (~17:30).

place.name: Lake Kawaguchiko & Oishi Park
place.summary: The classic northern Fuji viewpoint. Oishi Park’s lakeside promenade frames Fuji across the water — one of Japan’s most photographed compositions.
highlights: Oishi Park seasonal flower fields (cosmos often in early Oct)
tips: Check isfujivisible.com the night before — if visibility is “Poor”, swap to backup Day 3
Lake area is 5–10°C cooler than Tokyo — bring windbreaker
Morning 7:00–10:00 has best Fuji visibility; clouds often obscure by midday
place.photoNote: ★ Photo-heavy zone — budget 2+ hrs if conditions are clear. If Fuji is hidden, spend less time and explore lakeside cafés.
place.paceNote: If visibility is poor, accept it gracefully — lakeside is still pleasant but consider shortening to 1 hr.

place.name: Chureito Pagoda (Arakurayama Sengen Park)
place.summary: The iconic five-story pagoda with Fuji behind it — 398 steps up. One of the most famous views in Japan.
highlights: Seasonal cherry blossoms (not Oct) / early autumn tones
tips: 398 steps — seniors can wait at the base while others climb (partial views still exist lower down)
Free entry; can be crowded mid-morning on clear days
Combine with Shimoyoshida station (Fujikyu line)
place.photoNote: Allow 30+ min for the perfect shot — viewpoint gets crowded. Weekday helps.
place.paceNote: Recommend: young adults hike up, seniors rest at Fujisan Station café area if needed.

place.name: Kawaguchiko town & souvenir strip
place.summary: Lakefront shops, local Hoto noodle restaurants, and souvenir hunting. Relaxed fallback if weather turns.
tips: Buy return bus ticket early — evening buses sell out on clear Fuji days

meal.name: Hoto Fudo or Kawaguchiko Hoto
meal.note: Thick miso noodles in a hot pot — warming after lakeside wind. Famous rustic venues near the lake.

pokemonCenter.name: Pokemon Center SKYTREE TOWN
pokemonCenter.note: After Senso-ji morning exploration — 15 min walk or 1 stop on Asakusa Line to Oshiage.

place.name: Senso-ji Temple
place.summary: Tokyo’s oldest temple — thunder gate (Kaminarimon), Nakamise shopping street, and the main hall. The spiritual heart of Asakusa.
tips: Arrive 6:30–7:30 for fewer crowds and soft morning light — best for photos
Main hall open 6:00–17:00 (Oct)
Draw an omikuji fortune (¥100) — fun group activity
Imperial Palace East Gardens are CLOSED Fridays — good day for Asakusa instead
place.photoNote: ★★ Major photo day. Budget 2–3 hrs. Nakamise can eat another hour if you browse every stall.
place.paceNote: Speed-up tip: Focus on Kaminarimon → main hall → pagoda. Skip deep Nakamise browsing to save 45 min.

place.name: Sumida Park & river views
place.summary: Riverside walk with Skytree backdrop — good angle for tower + temple area context shots.
tips: Optional short river cruise from Asakusa pier if legs need a rest (~15 min)

place.name: Tokyo Skytree Town (exterior)
place.summary: Browse Solamachi mall at the base — Pokemon Center is here. Skytree observation deck is optional (not a priority vs Shibuya Sky).
tips: Observation deck ticket not essential — you visit Shibuya Sky for sunset views

ticket.detail: Deck: book ahead if desired; mall free

meal.name: Age.3 ASAKUSA
meal.note: From your saved list. Viral cream puffs — go early before sell-out. Perfect post-temple treat.

meal.name: Maguro-to-Shari Asakusa
meal.note: From your saved list. Fresh tuna specialist — lunch sets are excellent value.

meal.name: Magurobito Asakusa
meal.note: Budget-friendly alternative to Maguro-to-Shari — generous tuna bowls and sashimi sets without the longest queues. Good backup if Maguro-to-Shari is packed.

meal.name: Ichiran Asakusa
meal.note: Alternative lunch. Solo booth format — group sits in separate stalls. Note from your list: many Ichiran branches exist; this one pairs with Asakusa day.

meal.name: Dotombori Kamukura — Asakusa ROX
meal.note: From your saved list. Solid backup dinner near Asakusa station.

place.name: Nezu Shrine
place.summary: A hidden gem with a tunnel of vermillion torii gates — reminiscent of Fushimi Inari but far less crowded. Azalea festival is April; October offers moss, lanterns, and tranquil gardens.
highlights: Historic main hall (National Important Cultural Property)
tips: Opens at 6:00 — arrive 8:00 for best light + fewer Saturday crowds
10 min walk from Nezu Station (Chiyoda Line)
Combine with Yanaka — 15 min walk north
place.photoNote: Torii tunnel is narrow — patient queueing for photos. Allow 45+ min for photography.

place.name: Yanaka Ginza & district
place.summary: “Old Tokyo” survived the firebombing — wooden houses, temple cemeteries, artisan shops, and the famous Yanaka Ginza shopping street. Cats are unofficial mascots.
highlights: Yanaka Cemetery — peaceful tree-lined walks (respectful, quiet photos only)
tips: Yanaka Ginza gets busy weekends after 11:00 — go earlier
Cash useful at small shops
Many stairs in side alleys — seniors may prefer main Yanaka Ginza flat street
place.photoNote: Charming retro streetscapes — budget extra time. Sunset cat-themed snacks (menchi-katsu) are famous.
place.paceNote: Speed-up: Walk Yanaka Ginza main strip only (~45 min) to save energy for museum.

place.name: Tokyo National Museum
place.summary: Japan’s oldest and largest art museum — samurai armour, ukiyo-e prints, ceramics, and Buddhist sculpture. Honkan (Japanese Gallery) is the essential wing.
highlights: Honkan — Japanese art through the ages
tips: Closed Mondays — Saturday open 9:30–17:00
Seniors 70+ and under-18 free with passport/ID
Buy online ticket to skip queue
Wheelchairs available — mostly flat within buildings
place.paceNote: Focus on Honkan only (~90 min) if tired rather than all buildings.

place.name: Ueno Park
place.summary: Stroll through the park connecting museum, Shinobazu Pond, and Ueno Zoo exterior paths.
tips: Early Oct: still mostly green — peak autumn colour comes mid-Nov

meal.name: Yanaka Ginza — menchi-katsu / croquettes
meal.note: Famous meat croquettes — eat while walking the shotengai.

meal.name: Uogashi Nihon-Ichi Ueno Okachimachi
meal.note: Light sashimi lunch after the museum — same affordable standing-sushi chain as Day 1 if you skipped it earlier.

meal.name: Ueno area izakaya or café
meal.note: Many options near Ueno Station — or return to Gyukatsu Motomura if you loved it.

pokemonCenter.name: Pokemon Center SHIBUYA
pokemonCenter.note: First stop — then Meiji Shrine → Harajuku → Shibuya crossing → Sky for sunset.

place.name: Meiji Jingu
place.summary: A forest shrine oasis in the city — towering trees, massive torii, and peaceful paths. Recommended add-on near Shibuya day.
tips: Opens at sunrise (~5:30 in Oct) — shrine grounds always accessible
Flat main path — good for seniors; side gardens have more walking
Sunday mornings can have wedding processions — photogenic
place.photoNote: Forest light dappling — beautiful but dark under canopy. Big torii at entrance is the hero shot.

place.name: Shibuya Scramble Crossing
place.summary: The world’s busiest pedestrian crossing — up to 3,000 people per green light. View from ground level AND Shibuya Sky above.
highlights: Cross at street level for the experience
tips: Shibuya Sky covers the aerial view — ground crossing complements it
Magnet by Shibuya Station Tsutaya 2F is a classic overhead photo spot (free)
Return after Shibuya Sky (~18:30) for neon photos

place.name: Shibuya Sky
place.summary: 360° open-air rooftop 229m above Shibuya — the headline sunset experience. Watch Tokyo transition from golden hour to neon.
highlights: Open-air Sky Edge corner — iconic photo spot
Mt. Fuji silhouette on clear winter days (rare in Oct but possible at dusk)
360° city panorama including Shibuya crossing below
tips: ★ BOOK IN ADVANCE — sunset slot 16:00–16:30 entry for 17:20 sunset
Bring ¥100 coin for locker (bags not allowed on rooftop)
No tripods/selfie sticks on roof — phone only
Rooftop closes in high wind/rain — no refund; check forecast
Can stay past your slot until closing — no time limit once inside

ticket.detail: ¥2,700–3,400 online — book 28 days ahead at midnight JST

place.photoNote: ★★★ Top photo moment of the trip. Arrive 30 min before sunset. Windy — secure hats.

meal.name: Spontini Cascade Harajuku
meal.note: From your saved list. Thick Milanese-style slices — quick lunch between Meiji and Shibuya.

meal.name: Sushi no Midori Shibuya
meal.note: Famous budget sushi — generous lunch sets with sashimi. Expect 30–60 min queue at peak; go before noon or late afternoon. Great value alternative to Spontini if you prefer Japanese.

meal.name: Ramen Afro Beats Shinjuku
meal.note: From your saved list. Post-sunset dinner — 2 stops from Shibuya on JR.

meal.name: Izumo Shinjuku
meal.note: Alternative dinner from saved list. Lively izakaya — good for groups, reserve if possible.

place.name: Imperial Palace East Gardens
place.summary: The Edo Castle ruins transformed into imperial gardens — stone walls, moats, manicured lawns, and the foundation of the former keep. Free and tranquil.
highlights: Tenshudai (castle keep foundation) — elevated city views
tips: CLOSED Mondays & Fridays — Tuesday 7 Oct is OPEN
Oct hours: 9:00–16:30, last entry 16:00
Enter via Otemon Gate — flat paths, good for seniors
Peak autumn foliage here is late Nov — expect green in early Oct

ticket.detail: Free — pick up entry slip at gate

place.photoNote: Wide garden compositions — less crowded than Senso-ji. Morning light on stone walls is best.

place.name: Ginza district stroll
place.summary: Upscale shopping boulevard — flagship stores, art deco buildings, and people-watching. Window shopping is free entertainment.
tips: Most shops open 11:00 — morning is for architecture walks

place.name: Akihabara TCG district
place.summary: Electric Town’s card shop cluster — Hareruya2 Tower (6 floors), Poketown, Ninnin, and dozens more. Your main Pokemon card hunting ground beyond official Centers.
highlights: Hareruya2 Akihabara Tower — largest Pokemon TCG store
tips: Poketown opens 12:00 — do Imperial Palace & Ginza first
Hareruya open 10:00–22:00 — start here if Poketown not yet open
Tax-free at Poketown — bring passport
Compare prices — Hareruya singles often better value than sealed at PC
place.photoNote: Neon signs and multi-floor shops — fun documentary shots. Focus on shopping first.

meiji.text:
OPTIONAL if tired. Otherwise maybe before pokemon center or after pokemon center. 
Otherwise just shop around shibuya!

place.name: Nikko Toshogu Shrine
place.summary: Japan’s most lavish shrine — gold leaf, carvings of the “see no evil” monkeys, and the tomb of Tokugawa Ieyasu. A masterpiece of Edo craftsmanship.
tips: Many stairs throughout — seniors may prefer main courtyard level
Admission ~¥1,300 (often included in tours)
Early October: beginning of autumn colour at shrine cedar grove

ticket.detail: Usually bundled in tour; solo entry ¥1,300

place.photoNote: Detailed carvings reward close-up photography — allow time at Yomeimon.

place.name: Kegon Falls
place.summary: 97m waterfall at Lake Chuzenji outlet — one of Japan’s three finest falls. Elevator to observation platform.
tips: Elevator ¥570 — often included in tours
Cooler at altitude — extra layer

place.name: Lake Chuzenji & Irohazaka
place.summary: Mountain lake at 1,269m elevation — scenic drive via Irohazaka’s 48 hairpin turns. Akechidaira ropeway optional on some tours.
tips: Long bus day (~3 hrs each way from Tokyo) — bring neck pillow
Motion sickness sufferers: sit front of bus on Irohazaka

meal.name: Tour-provided stops or local Nikko yuba
meal.note: Nikko specialty is yuba (tofu skin). Tours usually stop at a restaurant or convenience area.

meal.name: TAMAGO-KEN Ikebukuro
meal.note: From saved list — if tour returns by ~18:00. Famous fluffy omurice near Ikebukuro Station.

pokemonCenter.name: Pokemon Center Tokyo Station & Tokyo DX
pokemonCenter.note: After Imperial Palace — 10 min from Otemachi. Tokyo Station store (10:00) then Tokyo DX (10:30); ~10 min walk between.

meal.name: Age.3 GINZA
meal.note: From saved list. Second Age.3 location — snack between Palace and Akihabara.

meal.name: Ginza Kagari — Soba
meal.note: From saved list. Famous rich chicken broth soba — expect 30–60 min queue. Split: 2 queue, 2 explore Ginza.

meal.name: Sushizanmai Tsukiji Outer Market
meal.note: Tsukiji Outer Market is ~15 min from Ginza — fresh sashimi breakfast/lunch sets at counter seats. Arrive before 11:00 to avoid the worst crowds. Perfect pre-Akihabara lunch.

meal.name: Kanda Tamagoken Akihabara
meal.note: From saved list. Classic fluffy omurice — perfect post-card-shopping comfort food.

place.name: Airport transfer
place.summary: Depart Tokyo 08:00 — aim to leave Ueno by 05:00–05:30 for Narita (N'EX ~55 min) or 05:30 for Haneda (~45 min).
tips: Pre-book Narita Express or airport limousine bus
Konbini breakfast at station — nothing open early at airport Terminal 3 sometimes
Tax-free shopping at airport if needed
